T2.objective: Explore a two-pass AVX-512 argmin: first compute the global signed int32 minimum; then scan from index zero with vector equality comparisons to find the earliest matching element, extracting the lowest matching lane and handling a scalar tail. T3.objective: Explore a compiler-friendly scalar scan with a small fixed unroll factor and several independent (minimum value, earliest index) accumulators. Fold the accumulators with signed-value then lowest-index ordering; handle any remainder scalarly. Do not use explicit SIMD or parallel workers in this branch. Measure whether reduced loop-carried dependence helps on both random and decreasing inputs, after correctness checks.
T3.subject: Unrolled scalar argmin with independent accumulators

This adds memory traffic: random inputs can require a substantial second scan, and decreasing inputs can require nearly a full second pass, so performance remains uncertain.

retained: Compute the signed int32 minimum with AVX512F vector minimum operations, then reduce the vector lanes and handle the first-pass scalar tail.
Scan from index zero using AVX512F equality masks; choose the lowest matching lane and use scalar search for the tail.

mission.hypothesis: A scalar argmin has a loop-carried comparison and index dependency for every element. Tracking signed minima and their earliest indices per AVX-512 lane processes 16 values per vector while retaining the first-index tie rule. A scalar fallback handles short inputs and a scalar tail completes non-multiple-of-16 sizes; the target attribute requests AVX-512F locally for the supplied EPYC 9654 target.

retained: Maintain a signed minimum and corresponding earliest absolute index in each of 16 AVX-512 lanes across complete vectors.
Update lane minima and indices only when a strictly smaller value arrives, preserving earlier equal minima; compare lane results by value then index.
Use a scalar path below one full vector and a scalar tuple comparison for the remaining tail.

hypotheses.claim: Le scan scalaire à quatre accumulateurs mérite une confirmation distincte sur les deux motifs requis; le scan baseline, plus simple mais plus lent dans les mesures agrégées visibles, reste un contrôle utile.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Comparer baseline et T3 avec les cinq répétitions de confirmation, en rapportant séparément les temps random et décroissant et en vérifiant la correction sur chacun.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Écarter T3 si une vérification échoue ou si son temps confirmé ne bat pas le baseline sur l’un des deux motifs.

observations.claim: T3 est déclaré valide et correct. Les cinq cas de correction réussissent; les trois temps visibles, tous pour pattern=0, donnent une moyenne de 2,8135 µs.
Le baseline est déclaré correct avec une moyenne agrégée de 4,4632 µs; il sert de référence plus simple, mais les données visibles ne permettent pas une comparaison par motif.

uncertainties: Le motif 0 n’est pas associé explicitement à random ou décroissant dans les éléments visibles; aucune mesure distincte de T3 sur ces deux motifs ni confirmation indépendante n’est fournie.

contract.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Return the first index of the smallest signed int32 value among n=8192 values. Input has 64-byte alignment. Cover random, decreasing, equal, repeated minima and INT32 extrema. One core. Both random and decreasing inputs are benchmarked in final validation.
Edit only src/candidate.cpp. Keep extern C void run(const void*input1,const void*input2,void*output,int n,int parameter,int threads). Respect the threads argument as the CPU thread budget. Inputs are read-only and 64-byte aligned. Overwrite the full specified output on every call; no cached answers, external tools or libraries, filesystem, environment inspection, timing inspection or phase detection. Ordinary C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Do not modify the protected correctness or timing protocol. Scratch allocation inside run is allowed and included in timing. The harness measures native wall-clock time, excluding input generation, oracle and compilation. Search and confirmation use different seeds. Numerical tolerances are fixed. The optimized reference source is withheld. Choose topics independently, record failed attempts, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G.
